To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Amino acids regulate proteolytic systems through the activation or inhibition of proteolytic pathways.
amino acids regulate protein degradation in skeletal muscle by controlling autophagy and the ubiquitin proteolytic system.

1) the Apg system is involved in the regulation of autophagic sequestation of proteins, 2) this system is activated in skeletal muscle cells in response to amino acid deprivation, 3) the activation of Apg system is mediated by a cascade that includes PI3K III, 4) Apg system activation is required for the amino acid deprivation-induced increase in autophagic sequstration of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of skeletal muscle proteolytic systems by amino acids and their derivatives.
the regulation of proteolysis by the amino acids, and with the role of proteolysis in the pathophysiological conditions of muscle wasting, in particular, in kidney failure.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of muscle proteolysis and the role of these mechanisms in muscle wasting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acids are the major regulators of proteolysis in muscle.
amino acids are involved in the regulation of proteolysis in muscle by acting as signals for the activation of the autophagy-lysosome pathway.
the regulation of muscle proteolysis in response to amino acid deprivation is complex, and involves multiple proteolytic systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amino acid availability is a major factor that regulates the balance between synthesis and degradation of muscle protein.
amino acids regulate protein degradation in muscle by controlling autophagy.

amino acids regulate proteolysis in muscle cells by controlling the expression of proteolytic enzymes through a mTOR-dependent pathway and by regulating autophagic proteolysis through a PI3K III-dependent signaling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amino acids are not only essential to sustain protein synthesis but also to inhibit protein breakdown, and that amino acid deprivation activates autophagy and other proteolytic systems.
amino acids can regulate proteolysis in skeletal muscle by a number of mechanisms, and that these mechanisms may be different in normal and pathological conditions.
amino acids can regulate the activity of proteolytic enzymes in muscle cells, and that the regulation of these enzymes by amino acids is likely to involve multiple mechanisms.
